meta.parties: National Bank of India v. Stevenson

rules.statement: Under English law, a bank can charge compound interest on current accounts where the customer has acquiesced in such practice and there is an agreement to pay it or if it aligns with trade custom.
rules.supporting_quote: "While under the Roman-Dutch law compound Interest was not allowed, even though it had been expressly stipulated for, under 497 the English law it was allowed where, inter alia, there was an agreement, express or implied. to pay it, or where its allowance was in accordance with a custom of a particular trade or business."
